const patch = "*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: D:\Program\python\Dubbed\_docs\frontend-flows\05-account-linking.md
+# Flow 05: Explicit account linking
+
+Status: initial draft; not approved; owner decisions OPEN  
+Date: 2026-10-22 (Asia/Qyzylorda)  
+Mode: specification only; no implementation or delivery evidence  
+Authority: [shared frontend contract](00-shared-contract.md), latest owner answers, then retained [SPEC-001](../specifications/SPEC-001_dubbed_mvp.md) and [BR-001](../business-requirements/BR-001_custom_video_dubbing.md) where not superseded
+
+## 1. Purpose and boundary
+
+This flow explicitly links Google and verified email/password sign-in methods after ownership is proven, so both methods open one canonical account with one balance, one project library, and one welcome grant.
+
+A matching email is only a candidate signal. It must never sign a person in, link methods, merge accounts, move projects or credits, or issue another welcome grant by itself.
+
+This flow covers the user-visible linking transaction, proof states, conflicts, cancellation, interruption, and safe return. It does not define a vendor OAuth API, password policy, email delivery, registration completion, password reset, account settings, unlinking, account merging, or conflict resolution between two existing account records.
+
+Optional unlinking is not approved. Flow 15 owns any future account-method management policy.
+
+## 2. Account identity invariant
+
+- A canonical account is identified by an internal account identity, not by displayed email text.
+- Google and email/password are sign-in methods associated with that canonical account.
+- The identity service is authoritative for method association, email verification, account status, and link eligibility.
+- Successful linking adds one method association to the already selected canonical account.
+- It does not create a second account, copy or sum balances, duplicate projects, duplicate purchases, or reassess welcome-credit eligibility.
+- A normalized or exact email match never proves ownership.
+- The happy path requires one canonical account plus a candidate method that is eligible to be linked.
+- If the candidate method is already attached to another canonical account, the operation is a conflict and performs no mutation. Resolution is `BLOCKED` by OPEN-F05-Q2.
+- If Google and email/password expose different verified emails, linking eligibility is `BLOCKED` by OPEN-F05-Q3.
+- Disabled, deleted, unverified, or otherwise ineligible identities cannot be made eligible by client-side state.
+
+## 3. Entry and exit
+
+### 3.1 Entry
+
+- Flow 02 detects that an attempted Google or email/password sign-in needs explicit linking before account entry.
+- Flow 03 finishes verified-email registration proof and receives an authoritative `link_required` continuation rather than creating or merging an account.
+- Flow 04 completes recovery needed to prove the email/password method, then returns only if the link intent is still eligible.
+- Flow 15 lets an authenticated owner select **Link** for an unassociated supported method.
+- Reload, Back, Forward, or a later authenticated return may resume only a still-valid server-owned link intent.
+
+Entry context may include an opaque link-operation identifier, intended canonical account, initiating method, candidate method, safe return destination, locale, expiry, and account revision. It must not include provider tokens, passwords, email proof secrets, or private account data in user-visible URLs or logs.
+
+### 3.2 Exit
+
+| Outcome | Exit |
+|---|---|
+| Linked | Reconcile authoritative account/method state, then return to the validated origin: Flow 02 session entry or Flow 15 Account. |
+| Cancelled before mutation | Return to the initiating flow; neither method nor account data changes. |
+| Proof denied or failed | Stay in recovery or return to Flow 02/03/04 as appropriate; no link occurs. |
+| Link intent expired or revoked | Show restart actions; never reuse cached eligibility. |
+| Existing-account or email conflict | Show a non-destructive blocked state governed by OPEN-F05-Q2/Q3. |
+| Session expired or account changed | Stop the transaction and hand off to Flow 02; do not disclose or mutate the previous account. |
+| Outcome unknown | Keep a neutral pending/unknown state and reconcile by operation identifier before offering mutation again. |
+
+New dub, project, recording, result, credit purchase, and account deletion behavior are outside this flow.
+
+## 4. Design application
+
+Both required design skills are applied as analysis guidance, not owner approval.
+
+- Treat linking as a sparse identity form inside the product, not a marketing page or dashboard.
+- Use the shared light rehearsal-room direction: white/light-gray flat surfaces, readable black text, and red only for actionable errors.
+- Use the compact top navigation for an authenticated owner and the shared authentication header when proof temporarily leaves the authenticated shell; never add a sidebar.
+- Keep one narrow reading column, one noun title, and one primary action per state.
+- Show the two methods as plain labeled rows with text status. Do not use icon-topped cards, security illustrations, gradients, glow, glass, confetti, or ornamental badges.
+- Google may use its approved provider mark only when brand guidance is available; otherwise the text label **Google** is sufficient.
+- Labels sit above fields; placeholders do not replace labels.
+- Exact font, hex values, dimensions, spacing, radii, breakpoints, routes, icons, and motion remain OPEN in the shared visual contract.
+- No random design draw or skill default selects those open decisions.
+
+## 5. Screen and component anatomy
+
+### 5.1 Shared header
+
+- Dubbed wordmark/home action.
+- English/Russian language control.
+- Safe back or cancel action appropriate to the origin.
+- Authenticated product navigation only when the current session may safely expose it.
+
+Changing locale updates all visible labels, status, help, errors, dialogs, and accessible names without discarding a valid service-owned link intent.
+
+### 5.2 Link overview
+
+Required content:
+
+- title: **Link sign-in methods** / **Связать способы входа**;
+- one sentence explaining that both methods will open the same account;
+- Google row with authoritative candidate/associated/proof status;
+- email/password row with authoritative verified/associated/proof status;
+- a compact statement that the account keeps its existing balance, projects, and single welcome grant;
+- one explicit **Continue linking** / **Продолжить привязку** action when eligible;
+- **Cancel** / **Отмена**.
+
+The screen must not suggest that matching email already linked the methods. It must not expose whether another private account exists beyond the disclosure policy selected for conflicts.
+
+### 5.3 Current-account proof
+
+The exact proof sequence is `BLOCKED` by OPEN-F05-Q1.
+
+The UI must be able to represent:
+
+- why confirmation is needed;
+- which current account is being protected, using only approved disclosure;
+- Continue to the required current-method reauthentication when selected;
+- pending, denied, cancelled, expired, rate-limited, and unavailable states;
+- a return that proves the same intended account, not merely any successful sign-in.
+
+If the owner selects active-session assurance without current-method reauthentication, the service still decides whether the session is sufficiently recent and eligible. The client cannot infer that assurance from a stored boolean.
+
+### 5.4 Candidate-method proof
+
+For Google, the visible action is **Continue with Google** / **Продолжить с Google** and returns an authoritative provider-proof result through the identity service.
+
+For email/password, the proof must refer to a verified email/password identity. Password entry uses a visible label, password-manager support, paste support, an accessible show/hide control, and no secret retention or logging.
+
+If email verification is incomplete, hand off to Flow 03. If password recovery is needed, hand off to Flow 04. Those flows return to this link intent only after their own authoritative success and a fresh eligibility check.
+
+Whether a Google-only owner may create a new password here, rather than link an existing verified email/password method, is not approved by this draft and must be resolved through Flow 03/04 ownership.
+
+### 5.5 Final review and submit
+
+Before mutation, show:
+
+- the two method families being linked;
+- the canonical account identifier allowed by the disclosure policy;
+- **Link methods** / **Связать способы** as the final action;
+- **Cancel** / **Отмена**;
+- a concise consequence: both methods will open the same existing account, balance, and projects.
+
+The final action submits one operation bound to the intended account, candidate method, verified proof context, expected account revision, and operation identifier.
+
+### 5.6 Success
+
+Required content:
+
+- **Sign-in methods linked** / **Способы входа связаны**;
+- Google and email/password shown as associated;
+- confirmation that the existing account, balance, projects, and one welcome grant were retained;
+- one next action determined by the validated origin.
+
+Do not claim a balance amount, project count, or grant state unless returned by the authoritative account snapshot.
+
+## 6. Main and alternate transitions
+
+### 6.1 Main path
+
+1. An originating flow receives an authoritative `link_required` result.
+2. The link overview loads the current operation and account-method snapshot.
+3. The user explicitly chooses to continue; no email match triggers mutation.
+4. The user completes the current-account and candidate-method proofs selected in OPEN-F05-Q1.
+5. The client reloads eligibility and the expected account revision.
+6. The user activates **Link methods**.
+7. The service atomically associates the candidate method with the one canonical account or returns a typed non-success result.
+8. On success, the client replaces cached account/method/balance/library facts with the authoritative snapshot and follows the validated return destination.
+
+### 6.2 Cancel and denial
+
+- Cancel before final submission performs no link and consumes no welcome grant.
+- Closing a provider window, denying provider consent, or backing out of password proof returns to a recoverable proof state without reporting failure as success.
+- Repeated proof failure never falls back to email equality.
+- **Use another sign-in method** hands off to Flow 02 and abandons or preserves the link intent only according to its service status.
+
+### 6.3 Expired, used, or revoked proof
+
+- Do not submit linking after any required proof becomes expired, used, revoked, or bound to a different account.
+- Clear secret fields and provider artifacts from view state.
+- Offer **Try again** only by starting the appropriate fresh proof.
+- If the overall link intent expired, offer **Back to sign in** or **Back to Account**; do not silently create another intent.
+
+### 6.4 Existing association and conflict
+
+- If both methods are already associated with the intended canonical account, reconcile to success without issuing another mutation or grant.
+- If the candidate becomes linked to another account before submit, stop and show the conflict state.
+- Never auto-merge two existing accounts, balances, libraries, purchases, grants, or account histories.
+- Self-service recovery, a separate merge process, or support handling for that conflict is `BLOCKED` by OPEN-F05-Q2.
+- Different verified emails are `BLOCKED` by OPEN-F05-Q3 and must not be silently accepted or rewritten.
+
+### 6.5 Stale state, concurrency, and unknown outcome
+
+- A stale account revision reloads the authoritative snapshot and requires fresh review.
+- A different account signed in in another tab invalidates the continuation.
+- Duplicate activation while pending is prevented locally, but backend idempotency remains required.
+- After timeout or lost response, query operation status before offering another final submission.
+- If status cannot be obtained, state that linking could not yet be confirmed; do not claim either success or failure.
+- A late success must reconcile to the canonical account only when the active session is authorized to receive it.
+
+### 6.6 Reload and resume
+
+- Reload reconstructs the flow from a server-owned operation and authoritative session, not component memory.
+- Resume requires the same intended canonical account, an unexpired link intent, and proof states the service still accepts.
+- Passwords and provider tokens are never restored.
+- Back/Forward after success cannot restore an actionable final-submit form.
+- A return from Flow 03 or 04 rechecks link eligibility before showing review.
+- Exact link-intent lifetime and allowed cross-device resume are security decisions within OPEN-F05-Q1; this draft promises neither.
+
+## 7. Loading, validation, and failure states
+
+| State | Visible behavior | Protection |
+|---|---|---|
+| Initial loading | Stable title/method-row structure with flat placeholders | No guessed association or account facts |
+| Proof pending | Plain progress text on the active proof action | Other final actions unavailable |
+| Invalid input | Field-associated message and focus on first invalid field | Safe typed fields retained; secrets not echoed |
+| Provider denied | Explain that Google verification was not completed; offer Retry or Cancel | No link and no account disclosure |
+| Verification incomplete | Route to Flow 03 with a validated continuation | No link before verified completion |
+| Password recovery needed | Route to Flow 04 without implying ownership | No link before fresh proof |
+| Rate limited | Show safe retry guidance only when supplied by service | No fabricated countdown |
+| Service unavailable | Keep non-secret context, show Retry | No success claim or blind mutation retry |
+| Intent expired | State that linking must restart | No cached proof reuse |
+| Conflict | State that methods could not be linked and show owner-selected recovery | No merge or data movement |
+| Outcome unknown | Explain that status is being checked | Reconcile operation before resubmit |
+
+## 8. Responsive, keyboard, and accessibility behavior
+
+### Desktop and tablet
+
+- Use the compact shared top navigation and a bounded single-column identity form.
+- Keep explanation, method statuses, proof controls, and actions in one reading order.
+- No sidebar, promotional rail, illustration, or unrelated product data appears.
+
+### Phone
+
+- Use 16–20 px outer margins as a target pending shared geometry.
+- Stack labels above fields and method status/actions vertically.
+- Touch targets are at least 44 px tall.
+- Provider handoff, errors, and actions must remain usable above safe areas and the software keyboard.
+- No horizontal page scroll at 390 px or with long Russian copy.
+
+### Keyboard and assistive technology
+
+- Order: header, title/instruction, method statuses, proof controls, final action, secondary actions.
+- Every control has a visible focus state and persistent accessible name.
+- Enter submits only the currently eligible form; it never skips review or launches two proof methods.
+- State changes are announced without repeated focus theft.
+- Field errors are programmatically associated; summary errors point to the affected step.
+- Provider-window cancellation returns focus to its initiating control.
+- Dialogs, if later required, have an accessible name, focus containment, Escape/Cancel before mutation, and correct focus return.
+- Color is never the only status or error signal; reduced motion removes unnecessary travel.
+
+## 9. Visible copy and localization
+
+| English | Russian |
+|---|---|
+| Link sign-in methods | Связать способы входа |
+| Continue linking | Продолжить привязку |
+| Continue with Google | Продолжить с Google |
+| Email and password | Электронная почта и пароль |
+| Verify email | Подтвердить почту |
+| Reset password | Сбросить пароль |
+| Link methods | Связать способы |
+| Sign-in methods linked | Способы входа связаны |
+| Nothing has been linked yet | Способы входа пока не связаны |
+| Linking could not be confirmed | Не удалось подтвердить привязку |
+| Try again | Повторить |
+| Back to sign in | Вернуться ко входу |
+| Back to Account | Вернуться в аккаунт |
+| Cancel | Отмена |
+
+Final disclosure, proof, conflict, mismatch, and recovery copy remains blocked by OPEN-F05-Q1/Q2/Q3 and requires security and localization review. Google remains the provider product name in both locales.
+
+## 10. Logical service flow
+
+These names describe responsibilities and result categories, not approved endpoints, schemas, libraries, or vendor APIs.
+
+| Logical operation | Inputs | Required results |
+|---|---|---|
+| `startLinkIntent` | authenticated/session context, origin, desired method, locale | eligible intent, reauthentication required, unverified, conflict, denied, unavailable |
+| `loadLinkIntent` | opaque operation identity and current session | current snapshot, expired, revoked, wrong account, completed, unavailable |
+| `proveCurrentAccount` | intent and owner-selected proof | verified, denied, expired, rate limited, unavailable |
+| `proveCandidateMethod` | intent and Google or verified email/password proof | verified, unverified, denied, expired, already associated here/elsewhere, mismatch, unavailable |
+| `commitMethodLink` | intent, both required proof results, expected account revision, idempotency identity | linked snapshot, already linked here, stale, conflict, expired/revoked, unknown, unavailable |
+| `getLinkStatus` | operation identity and authorized session | pending, linked snapshot, not linked, conflict, expired/revoked, unavailable |
+
+The centralized service boundary is interchangeable. Zustand may coordinate display state but is not authority for identity, proof validity, association, canonical account selection, balance, project library, grant eligibility, or operation outcome.
+
+### Mock-truth boundary
+
+A mock may deterministically simulate matching emails, all proof results, delay, denial, expiry, stale revision, conflict, duplicate submit, unknown outcome, and successful reconciliation.
+
+A mock cannot prove:
+
+- live Google identity or provider consent;
+- mailbox or password ownership;
+- token integrity, audience, nonce, replay resistance, expiry, or revocation;
+- real account uniqueness, atomic linking, idempotency, or concurrent-write protection;
+- preservation of production balances, projects, purchases, grants, sessions, or audit records;
+- account-enumeration resistance, abuse prevention, or provider availability.
+
+Every mock Google/email interaction and UI check must be labeled simulation, not backend, provider, production-data, or security evidence.
+
+## 11. Privacy and persistence boundaries
+
+- Passwords, provider tokens, proof secrets, security claims, and recovery artifacts never appear in URLs, analytics, user-visible logs, or persisted client stores.
+- Persist only the minimum opaque operation context needed by the approved resume contract.
+- Link audit data and proof retention belong to the future security/backend contract; this draft does not set duration.
+- Private account existence, method state, email, balance, projects, and grant eligibility must not leak through public errors.
+- Cached private snapshots are cleared or replaced when the session expires, the active account changes, or authoritative linking succeeds.
+- Linking does not alter project, recording-draft, result, sharing, credit-expiry, or account-deletion retention rules.
+
+## 12. Acceptance criteria
+
+All criteria are unexecuted. `BLOCKED` identifies a required owner/security decision.
+
+- [ ] **F05-AC01 — Explicit intent:** an email match may create only a candidate `link_required` state; no sign-in, association, merge, data move, or grant occurs before explicit final action and required proofs.
+- [ ] **F05-AC02 — Unique canonical account:** success associates Google and verified email/password with exactly one canonical account and returns its one balance, project library, and welcome-grant state without duplication.
+- [ ] **F05-AC03 — Proof:** current-account and candidate-method proof states cover pending, denial, cancellation, expiry, rate limiting, and unavailability. **BLOCKED by OPEN-F05-Q1.**
+- [ ] **F05-AC04 — Existing-account conflict:** a method already associated elsewhere never auto-merges accounts or moves balances/libraries/grants. **Recovery is BLOCKED by OPEN-F05-Q2.**
+- [ ] **F05-AC05 — Email mismatch:** different-email cases never silently link or rewrite identifiers. **Eligibility and copy are BLOCKED by OPEN-F05-Q3.**
+- [ ] **F05-AC06 — Cancel and expiry:** cancellation, denial, expired proof, and expired intent perform no link and return through a safe stated path.
+- [ ] **F05-AC07 — Concurrency:** duplicate clicks, stale revisions, account switching, already-linked races, timeout, reload, and late results reconcile one idempotent operation without a blind retry.
+- [ ] **F05-AC08 — Resume:** only the same authorized account can resume a valid intent; secrets are never restored, and completed history cannot restore the final-submit form. **Cross-device/lifetime details are BLOCKED by OPEN-F05-Q1.**
+- [ ] **F05-AC09 — Handoffs:** Flow 02 reauthentication, Flow 03 verification, Flow 04 recovery, and Flow 15 return preserve the intended account and recheck eligibility.
+- [ ] **F05-AC10 — Bilingual accessibility:** complete English/Russian states work on desktop, tablet, 390 px phone, keyboard, screen reader, 200% zoom, reduced motion, and short viewports without mixed-language or clipped actions.
+- [ ] **F05-AC11 — Privacy:** secrets and private account existence stay out of URLs, analytics, persisted client state, and disclosure beyond the approved policy.
+- [ ] **F05-AC12 — Honest evidence:** mock states are identified as simulation and never presented as proof of Google, email/password, backend security, atomicity, or production-data preservation.
+- [ ] **F05-AC13 — Visual contract:** rendered states use the approved shared light/flat tokens, compact top navigation, form hierarchy, and no gradients/sidebar. **BLOCKED until shared tokens/geometry and rendered evidence exist.**
+
+## 13. Verification plan — not executed
+
+1. Review the flow against the shared contract, SPEC-001, BR-001, and resolved owner answers.
+2. Contract-test every logical result category, including same-account already-linked, other-account conflict, mismatched email, stale revision, and unknown outcome.
+3. Component-test main, cancel, denial, expiry, unavailable, conflict, reload, and success states with deterministic fixtures in English and Russian.
+4. Exercise entry and return handoffs with Flows 02, 03, 04, and 15, including expired session and a different active account.
+5. Exercise duplicate final activation, response loss before/after commit, reload while pending, late provider return, and another-device association.
+6. Verify that no email equality path invokes link commit and that no conflict fixture moves or combines balances, libraries, purchases, or grants.
+7. Inspect final renders at desktop, tablet, and 390 px with long Russian copy, 200% zoom, short height, keyboard open, and safe-area insets.
+8. Run keyboard-only and screen-reader checks for status announcements, field errors, provider-return focus, cancellation, and success navigation.
+9. Inspect URLs, storage, logs, analytics payloads, and error copy for password/provider/proof secrets and private-account disclosure.
+10. With real services only, verify live provider proof, replay/expiry handling, atomic association, account uniqueness, idempotency, concurrent updates, and preservation of production account data.
+11. Record command, environment, date, revision or dirty-worktree boundary, result, and evidence location; mark blocked or not run honestly.
+
+No verification, browser run, provider request, email delivery, backend call, or security test was executed by this specification authoring pass.
+
+## 14. Dependencies and handoffs
+
+| Dependency | Responsibility |
+|---|---|
+| Shared contract / Flow 01 | Product identity, compact navigation, locale entry, responsive shell, eventual visual tokens |
+| Flow 02 — Sign in | Initial auth attempt, current-session resolution, reauthentication, safe signed-in destination |
+| Flow 03 — Registration and verification | Verified-email completion without implicit linking or duplicate account creation |
+| Flow 04 — Password reset | Recovery proof and fresh eligibility return; no implicit linking |
+| Flow 15 — Account | Authoritative method rows, Link entry, reconciled return; future unlink policy remains separate and unapproved |
+| Identity/account service | Canonical account, method association, proof eligibility, operation status, conflict result, revision fencing |
+| Balance/project/grant services | Authoritative unchanged account snapshot and safeguards against duplication or movement |
+| Security/privacy policy | Proof strength, intent lifetime/resume, disclosure, audit/retention, abuse and rate-limit rules |
+
+## 15. OPEN decisions and blockers
+
+| ID | Owner decision needed | Impact |
+|---|---|---|
+| OPEN-F05-Q1 | Require fresh proof of both the current and candidate methods; rely on the current session plus candidate proof; or vary proof by a separately defined assurance policy? Also define link-intent lifetime and resume scope. | Proof screens, session handoff, expiry, resume, F05-AC03/F05-AC08 |
+| OPEN-F05-Q2 | When the candidate method already belongs to another canonical account, block with recovery guidance, create a separately specified authenticated merge process, or route to an approved support channel? | Conflict disclosure/recovery, account uniqueness, F05-AC04 |
+| OPEN-F05-Q3 | Permit linking only when verified emails match, permit different verified emails after explicit proof, or block different-email linking for launch? | Eligibility, canonical account email/recovery semantics, copy, F05-AC05 |
+
+Until those answers exist, the draft does not choose proof strength, account merge/deduplication, different-email behavior, canonical-email priority, or support policy. It always forbids automatic linking and automatic merging.
+
+Shared exact typography, colors, measurements, routes, microinteractions, and any real provider/security contract remain OPEN. Optional unlinking remains outside this flow and awaits a separate owner decision in Flow 15.
+
+## 16. Design-skill application and evidence boundary
+
+The author applied `.agents/skills/design-taste-frontend/SKILL.md`, its app-screen and forms guidance, and `.agents/skills/frontend-design/SKILL.md`.
+
+They informed the sparse form hierarchy, noun title, flat surfaces, restrained status color, plain method rows, one primary action, honest loading/error states, phone stacking, visible focus, and direct action/result copy. The confirmed Dubbed direction overrides generic or randomly dealt style choices.
+
+The skills do not approve product behavior or visual tokens. No style draw, mockup, product code, screenshot, browser inspection, live provider flow, email delivery, account mutation, or backend/security evidence was produced.
*** End Patch";
text(await tools.apply_patch(patch));
